title: Python SDK conversational telemetry hooks and safe-split emit pattern
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Add a composable telemetry hook surface and a 'safe-split emit' pattern to the Python SDK streaming chat API so integrators can attach event-level metrics, persist resumable deltas, and emit partial conversation snapshots without risking message duplication or corrupted structured events.
proposed_solution: Introduce ConversationTelemetry and EmitCheckpoint primitives on the streaming response iterator. ConversationTelemetry exposes on_message, on_error, on_checkpoint, and on_commit callbacks that receive stable ids and watermark offsets. EmitCheckpoint is an idempotent small-snapshot emitter that returns a monotonic checkpoint token which the SDK will attach to subsequent retry/fallback attempts. The iterator will batch small writes to the telemetry sink and expose a backpressure handle so callers can await durable flush before acknowledging user-side side-effects.
implementation_notes: Add ConversationTelemetry dataclass with optional coroutine callbacks to the ChatStream API surface.
Enhance ChatStreamEvent objects with stable_event_id and watermark_offset strings to enable deduplication and ordering in sinks.
Implement EmitCheckpoint API backed by a lightweight retryable writer that uses exponential backoff and per-checkpoint idempotency tokens.
Wire a bounded async queue for telemetry writes that the SDK flushes before stream completion; expose flush() to callers for transactional handoffs.

Provide examples: (a) writing snapshot JSON to S3/GCS with checkpoint tokens, (b) sending minimal metrics to internal StatsD/Prometheus pushgateway, (c) using a database transactional upsert keyed by stable_event_id.
Document best practices and failure modes in the README + Console docs; include migration notes for existing telemetry hooks.
Add unit tests for checkpoint token uniqueness, retry surface on transient failures, and ordering guarantees under out-of-order event arrival.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes ConversationTelemetry on ChatClient.stream_chat that accepts coroutine callbacks for on_message/on_checkpoint/on_commit/on_error.
Each ChatStreamEvent contains stable_event_id and watermark_offset fields that are surfaced to telemetry callbacks and are stable across retries.
EmitCheckpoint returns a short opaque token and is idempotent: repeated calls with same token do not create duplicates in the example sink (unit/integration tests validate).
SDK provides flush_telemetry() that completes only after the bounded queue is drained or a configurable timeout, and is called automatically on graceful stream close.

Integration example: sample app persists incremental snapshots to object storage using EmitCheckpoint; after simulated SDK retries the snapshot is not duplicated and resumes from the last committed checkpoint.
Docs updated with code samples, migration guide, and recommended retry/backpressure settings.
test_plan: Unit tests: validate callback invocation ordering, checkpoint token format, and queue backpressure behavior.
Integration tests: run a local fake telemetry sink that intentionally drops connections; assert EmitCheckpoint retry and de-dup behavior.
E2E example: sample conversational agent persists snapshots to a sqlite test DB using stable_event_id; run scenario with mid-stream interruption and ensure resumed run does not duplicate rows.
Load test: emit telemetry at low, medium, high token rates to verify bounded queue prevents OOM and metrics show limited p99 latency impact on generator path.
Security: ensure tokens and checkpoint payloads do not leak sensitive prompt content; add a sanitizer hook that's used in telemetry examples.
risks: If checkpoint tokens are not globally unique across customers, sinks may accidentally dedupe unrelated streams — include customer-scoped namespace in tokens.
Backpressure could increase end-to-end latency if integrators misuse flush() synchronously; document async flows and provide sync helpers with timeouts.
Telemetry sinks may become a source of failures; ensure SDK can fall back to best-effort mode (drop + metric) and expose a 'strict' option for customers who require durability.
Complexity increase to the public API surface — need thorough docs and migration path to prevent developer confusion.
